leaveBehind: LESSON (gate-worthy): a 'is it identical to X' argument is only as durable as the measurement's date. The copies ARE identical today (fa8a30eaf4a3 / eac36569eb71) and would have looked identical forever if nobody wrote the check; scripts/check-staging-secret-drift.mjs is the difference between a fact and a standing fact, and its --selftest is what makes the indicator trustworthy before it is believed.

LESSON: an identity claim about a rotated secret must compare HASHES and the code path that mints the value. addSecretVersion creates a new VERSION on every reset while the VALUE repeats when the branch is restored in place -- so 'version 12 -> 17' is NOT evidence that the value moved, and 'byte-identical' has to be measured on the value, not inferred from the version count.

LESSON (gate-worthy): the reason a lane must not add a rotation target it cannot write is that a fail-closed write inside the reset job BLOCKS THE PUBLISH PATH IT PROTECTS. The grounding is one gcloud read (project IAM + secret IAM) -- measure the write identity's roles before adding a cross-project writer, not after.

DEAD-END: invoking gcloud from node on Windows must go through a shell. `execFileSync('gcloud', args)` fails with ENOENT (gcloud is gcloud.cmd/gcloud.ps1); `{ shell: true }` is required, as the drift check does (and as check-live-job-has-config.mjs already did). Discovered twice in this lane.

DEAD-END: don't build a node script's file paths with PowerShell string interpolation like "$inbox${pre}name" when $inbox has no trailing separator -- it silently creates files named `_inbox2026-...` in the parent directory. Five stray artifacts were created and removed in this lane; use Join-Path or explicit backslashes.
